interface.title: EspressoIn - Tools (Band Structure)
interface.field: Computational materials science / condensed-matter physics (DFT post-processing with Quantum ESPRESSO)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysing and presenting results after a band-structure calculation
interface.what_it_is_for: Visualise a Quantum ESPRESSO band-structure file as a figure: shift energies to the Fermi level, label high-symmetry k-points, print a band-gap readout, change the styling and export the image.

data.note: I uploaded sample_bands.dat.gnu (1.8 KB, 4 bands) through the 'Upload data file (data.dat.gnu)' uploader. With E_F = 0 or 0.5 the app reports 'Band Gap = 1.50 eV', which is the expected 1.5 eV. I also downloaded the app's own sample.dat (136 KB, a real QE file) from the how-to expander but did not plot it.

tree.specific: Plot a Quantum ESPRESSO bands .dat.gnu file relative to E_F, with high-symmetry k-labels and the band-gap readout, and export it as an image

features.name: Band-file loader and multi-band plotter
features.general: Upload a two-column result file (position along a path, energy). The tool splits it into separate curves and draws every curve as a line in a preview figure that all the other controls act on. Removing the file returns the tool to its empty state.
features.specific: The 'Upload data file (data.dat.gnu)' uploader takes a QE bands .dat.gnu file (k, E). According to the reviewer's reading of app.py, rows are split into separate bands wherever k resets to 0, every band is drawn in the 'Band Structure' Plot Preview, and the axis limits are fitted to the data. sample_bands.dat.gnu (4 bands) was plotted this way. The × on the file chip removes the plot and the Data/Customise/Download panels.
steps: Upload the .dat.gnu file
Scroll to the Plot Preview to see every band drawn
Optionally click × on the file chip to unload it
serves_tasks: Load a computed result file and see it plotted
Unload the data file and return to the empty state

features.name: Reference-level shift with nearest-point markers and gap readout
features.general: Enter a reference value. The curves are re-plotted relative to it. The nearest data points just below and just above the reference, pooled over all curves, are marked, and the gap between them is printed on the figure. This is the true gap only when the reference lies inside a gap. A reference inside a curve's range gives a spurious small value.
features.specific: Type the Fermi Energy (eV) or step it by 0.5. Bands are drawn as E − E_F with a dashed Fermi line, and dots mark the nearest points below and above E − E_F = 0 from all bands pooled together. 'Show Band Gap Energy Below Title' prints 'Band Gap = X eV'. With E_F inside the gap (0 or 0.5) the dots are the VBM and CBM and the readout is 1.50 eV. With E_F inside a band (1.0) the dots sit where bands cross E_F and the readout is a spurious 0.18 eV, not a metal flag (screens/042.webp).
steps: Upload the band-structure file
Type or step the Fermi Energy value
Watch the bands, Fermi line and nearest-point markers move
Tick 'Show Band Gap Energy Below Title' to print the readout under the title
Check that E_F lies inside the gap before trusting the value
serves_tasks: Set the reference energy so values are shown relative to it
Print on the figure the gap between the nearest data points just below and just above the reference level; this is a true band gap only when the reference lies inside a gap

features.name: Labelled x-axis markers from a count-driven list
features.general: Choose how many named positions to mark. For each, pick a name from a preset list or type your own, and give its x position. The axis gets those ticks and a vertical guide line at each.
features.specific: Number of High Symmetry Points creates one 'Label for Point n' dropdown (Γ, M, R, X, K, L, …, or Add Custom Label), one custom-label text box and one x-coordinate box per point. The x-axis ticks become Γ / X / W with vertical lines. Lowering the count removes the extra labels.
steps: Set Number of High Symmetry Points
Pick a preset label or type a custom label for each point
Enter each point's x-coordinate
Lower or raise the count to remove or add points
serves_tasks: Mark named positions along the x-axis

features.name: Live plot-styling panel
features.general: A side panel of styling controls whose every change redraws the preview straight away: grid, series colour and line width, highlight-marker colour and size, reference-line colour and width, tick spacing, title and axis labels.
features.specific: Customise Plot has Show Grid, 'Choose plot colour' (picker with hue slider and hex box), Line Thickness (Band Structure) 0.25–5, Dot Marker Colour, Marker Size 0–150, Line Colour and Line Thickness (Fermi Level), Y-axis Increment, Graph title, and x/y-axis Labels (matplotlib mathtext accepted).
steps: Open Customise Plot
Toggle the grid and the gap readout
Pick colours with the picker (drag the hue slider or type a hex code)
Drag or key the thickness and size sliders
Type the tick increment, title and axis labels
serves_tasks: Change line, marker and reference-line appearance and see the preview update
Set the axis tick spacing, title and axis labels

features.name: Figure export with format, DPI and file name
features.general: Choose an image format, a resolution and an optional file name (it defaults to the figure title), then save the current figure in two clicks.
features.specific: In Download Settings, set Image Resolution (DPI) and the format (jpg/png/tiff/svg) and optionally 'Enter Custom File Name'. Press Download Plot, which reveals 'Download as JPG/SVG/…', and press that to save.
steps: Open Download Settings
Set the DPI
Choose the format
Optionally type a file name
Press Download Plot, then 'Download as <FMT>'
serves_tasks: Save the figure as an image file in a chosen format and resolution

screens_never_reached: A plot of the app's own sample.dat (the real QE file from the how-to expander). I downloaded it but no tool lets me re-upload a downloaded file, and the only uploadable test file is sample_bands.dat.gnu.
not_done: Did not export png or tiff. Only jpg and svg were downloaded. The svg was read and carries the styling; the jpg is binary, so its contents were not checked beyond its size (178,735 bytes).
Did not check that the DPI value changes the output resolution. The SVG header shows 576x432 pt regardless.
Did not untick 'Show Band Gap Energy Below Title' a second time, and did not look at the help tooltips other than the Fermi Energy one.

Observed, not fixed: the band gap is computed from the nearest data points above and below E_F, pooled across all bands, not from the band structure itself. With E_F = 1.0 (inside the conduction band) it reports 0.18 eV instead of a metal or the 1.5 eV gap (screens/042.webp).

Observed, not fixed: the Plot Preview prints leftover debug output ('None' twice and lists of matplotlib XTick/Text objects) and a Streamlit deprecation warning about savefig kwargs above the plot (screens/011.webp, screens/045.webp).

Observed, not fixed: the custom-label text box takes priority, but while a point's dropdown still reads 'Add Custom Label' and its text box is empty, the literal text 'Add Custom Label' is drawn as an axis tick (screens/017.webp, screens/020.webp).

The sidebar title and blurb ('EspressoIn - Tools', 'Still under development!…') and the 'Select Language' label stay in English when another language is chosen; only the main content and the Settings heading are translated.
